sentences.text: I have heard the learned counsel appearing for petitioners-accused persons and the learned HCGP for respondent-state.

3. The genesis of the complaint is that on 13.09.2015 at about 8.00 a.m. when the complainant was in police station, he received a telephone call stating that accused No.2 and other accused are involved in manufacturing and adulteration of milk by mixing chemical powder and trying to sell the same to the public.
Immediately, the complainant along with his staff and pancha witnesses went to the said place and conducted a raid in the house of accused No.2.
At that time, accused No.1 was also present there.
There, they found one plastic bag, other materials and vehicles loaded with milk powders.
On verification, they found that the accused No.1 was using mixer and mixing the powder with oil and mixing the said mixture into milk to increase the quantity.
There were six empty cans which were kept for the purpose of filling the same.
On enquiry, they came to know that the accused persons were mixing the powder with oil and thereafter increasing the quantity of milk by mixing the water.
The said milk powder was intended to be supplied to Anganwadi schools in Karnataka.
On the basis of the complaint, cases have been registered against the petitioners-accused persons.

4. It is the submission of the learned counsel for petitioners-accused persons that the other accused have already been released on bail during the crime stage itself, and the charge-sheet has already been filed in both the cases.
On the ground of parity, these petitioners-accused persons are also entitled to bail.

It is submitted that the alleged offences are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life and the petitioners-accused persons are ready to abide by all the conditions imposed by this Court and also ready to furnish the surety to the satisfaction of the Court.
On these grounds, prayed to allow the petitions.

5. Per contra, the learned HCGP for respondent-state has vehemently argued and contended that the petitioners-accused persons along with accused Nos.1 and 2 have sold the milk which was intended to be supplied to Anganwadi schools by increasing the quantity by mixing oil and water in it.
The petitioners- accused persons were involved in serious offence, which would affect the health of general public as well as small children.

It is submitted that the petitioners-accused persons were absconding since from the date of incident and if they are released on bail, they may again abscond from the jurisdiction of trial court and they may not be available for trial.
On these grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. I have carefully and cautiously gone through the submissions made by the learned counsel for petitioners-accused persons and the learned HCGP for respondent-state and perused the records.

7. As could be seen from the contents of the complaint and other materials it shows that accused Nos. 1 to 5 were involved in preparing adulterated milk for the purpose of wrongful gain and it is alleged that the petitioners-accused persons were absconding from the date of incident and were not Sri.

sentences.text: When accused Nos.1 to 5 have already been enlarged on bail, on the ground of parity, the petitioners-accused persons are also entitled to be released on bail.
Whether the petitioners-accused persons were involved in the alleged crime or not is the matter which has to be considered and appreciated at the time of trial.

Taking into consideration the above said facts and circumstances, I feel that if the petitioners-accused persons are released on bail by imposing some stringent conditions on them, it would meet the ends of justice.

8. In that light, both the petitions are allowed and the petitioners herein/accused persons in both these petitions are enlarged on bail in the event of their arrest in C.C.No.355/2017 &
C.C.No.356/2017 on the file of the Prl. Civil judge & JMFC Court, Raibag registered for the offences punishable under sections 272, 273, 284, 328, 420 of IPC and Section 54, 57 & 59 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, arising out of Crime No.299/2015 and Crime No.298/2015 of Raibag Police Station, subject to following conditions:
i.
Each petitioner herein/accused persons shall execute personal bond for Rs.2,00,000/- with two sureties for like sum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer.
ii. They shall appear before the Investigating Officer within a period of 15 days from today.
iii. They shall mark their attendance before the Investigating Officer on the first day of every month till conclusion of the trial.
iv. They shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Court below without obtaining prior permission.
v. They shall not tamper with the  prosecution witnesses directly or  indirectly.
vi. They shall appear before this Court and the Court below as and when directed to do so.
